transcript.en: Nikole sits next to Najya, and they talk. I'm going to bleep the name of Najya's high school when it comes up in this conversation. They're sitting side by side, and Nikole begins laying out her case.
transcript.zh: Nikole 在 Najya 身边坐下，母女俩聊了起来。接下来的对话里每次提到 Najya 高中的校名，我都会做消音处理。她们并排坐着，Nikole 开始陈述自己的理由。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: She's clear, vulnerable, tells Najya this was a hard choice, the hardest choice. Najya still seems to be listening carefully. As Nikole says, public education is just so deeply unequal and always has been. Black kids in particular segregated and denied a fair and equal education.
transcript.zh: 她条理清晰又坦诚脆弱，告诉 Najya 这是一个艰难的决定，是最难的选择。Najya 看上去也一直在认真听。正如 Nikole 所说，公共教育体系本来就极其不平等，向来如此；尤其是黑人孩子，一直被隔离在外，得不到公平和平等的教育。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: What do we then do? Do we just say, well, there's nothing I can do? Or do you try in some way to make some intervention?
transcript.zh: 那我们该怎么办呢？难道就摊摊手说“算了，我也无能为力”吗？还是说，你总得想方设法去做出一点改变和干预？

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: It's like, why should my child be the one that's rescued? Like you should escape what we consign so many other kids just like you to? I just will never feel right about that.
transcript.zh: 就像我总在想，凭什么只有我的孩子能被“救”出去？凭什么只有你能够逃离那种困境，而我们却任由那么多跟你一模一样的孩子被困在里面？这种事，我心里永远过意不去。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Why? Why? It makes no sense. You're talking about, oh, I'm just going to give you the worst just because it's not fair that you—I didn't ask to be born. All you're supposed to do is just like...
transcript.zh: 为什么？凭什么呀？这根本说不通。你的意思不就是“哦，就因为别人过得不好不公平，所以我干脆也给你选最差的”——可又不是我求着要出生的。你作为家长，本该做的不就是……

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Put me in a good school. Like, oh, well, I didn't want to put you in a great school and have you have advantages over other kids.
transcript.zh: 送我去一所好学校啊。什么“哦，我可不想把你送进顶尖学校，让你比别的孩子占优势”。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Isn't that what you want? Isn't that what you want me to have? Is that not a normal thing you want me to have? You don't want me to have this—
transcript.zh: 难道那不正是你想要的吗？不就是你想让我拥有的吗？想让孩子拥有这些，难道不是人之常情吗？你难道不想让我——

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: You do, though.
transcript.zh: 可你确实拥有啊。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Okay, yeah, but—
transcript.zh: 好，是，但——

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: But you do. You have advantages. You have so many advantages.
transcript.zh: 你就是有。你有很多优势，非常多。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Right, okay, so—but I'm not seeing them. I'm saying school-wise. I'm in school every day. I was in that building every single day.
transcript.zh: 行，好吧，可我没感受到啊。我说的是学校方面。我每天都在上学，每一天都待在那个教学楼里。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: That doesn't make sense. I'm there more than home. Obviously, I get more in general, but school is the most important thing. That's the main thing.
transcript.zh: 这说不通啊。我在学校待的时间比在家还长。当然，我在其他方面是得到了更多，但学校才是最重要的，这才是最核心的。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Why do you imagine you're able to do well in [BLEEP]?
transcript.zh: 那你觉得，为什么你能在那所学校读得这么好呢？

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Um, because it's a better school.
transcript.zh: 嗯，因为那是所更好的学校。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: But you—do you think it's possible your foundation wasn't as terrible as you think it is?
transcript.zh: 但你有没有想过，也许你的基础并没有你自己以为的那么差？

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: No.
transcript.zh: 没有。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: So you think you came in like a blank slate at [BLEEP] and now have learned everything there?
transcript.zh: 所以你觉得你进那所学校时就像一张白纸，所有东西都是到了那儿才学的？

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: No, but—
transcript.zh: 也不是，但——

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: You have been able to have the same academic success as your classmates.
transcript.zh: 你在学业上完全跟得上同学，表现得一样出色。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Yeah, to get through it because—well, not even though. Last year, when I had my grade come out, I remember crying because everyone else's score was so good.
transcript.zh: 是啊，我能熬过来是因为——其实也谈不上。我记得去年成绩出来的时候，我哭了，因为其他所有人的分数都那么高。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And I was just like, how is this so easy for everyone else but me? So no, I don't think that I got through it. I think I just tried my hardest.
transcript.zh: 我当时就在想，为什么这对别人来说都那么轻而易举，偏偏就我这么难？所以不，我不觉得我是什么“熬过来了”，我只是拼尽了全力而已。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Yeah. I mean, I think it's fair to say you did not receive the top quality middle school education.
transcript.zh: 是。我觉得说实话，你在初中确实没有接受到最顶尖的教育。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Either in elementary with—
transcript.zh: 小学也没有，连——

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: That's fair.
transcript.zh: 说得对。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: —even basic fractions. I mean, I was never taught that. I had to relearn everything from my tutor.
transcript.zh: ——连最基础的分数都没学好。我根本没被教过那些，所有东西都得靠家教老师从头教起。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: That's fair.
transcript.zh: 这确实是事实。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Everyone's not your kid.
transcript.zh: 别人家的孩子又不是你的孩子。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: That's fair.
transcript.zh: 没错。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: You can't save everyone who doesn't want to be saved.
transcript.zh: 你救不了每一个不想被救的人。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Oh. That's what you think, though? You think other kids don't want better?
transcript.zh: 哦，你是这么想的吗？你觉得别的孩子不想要更好的教育吗？

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I'm not saying that. I wanted better. All the kids in my school that wanted better wanted better.
transcript.zh: 我不是那个意思。我也想要更好的。我学校里所有想变好的孩子都想要更好的。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: There's no benefit that came out of you putting me in those schools. There's no benefit at all. Could you tell me a benefit?
transcript.zh: 你把我送进那些学校，根本没带来任何好处。一点好处都没有。你能说出一个好处来吗？

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: You want me to answer that? Benefit for the school?
transcript.zh: 你想让我回答这个问题吗？对学校的好处？

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: What benefit did you provide the school?
transcript.zh: 你们给那所学校带来了什么好处？

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I think that's a great question. I do think it was a benefit of us being in those schools. We brought resources. If you remember—
transcript.zh: 我觉得这个问题问得很好。我确实认为我们在那些学校里是有帮助的。我们带去了资源。如果你还记得——

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: Nikole runs through a bunch of examples—your dad organizing parents at the school, intervening when there were issues with teachers, making sure kids who couldn't afford field trips would still get those opportunities.
transcript.zh: Nikole 一口气举了一连串例子——你爸爸在学校里组织家长，老师出问题时出面交涉，确保那些交不起钱参加校外研学的孩子也能获得同样的机会。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: The principal creating a recognition breakfast for kids who made the honor roll wouldn't have happened if you weren't in the school. Nikole goes big and specific. The benefits of kids having friends from different backgrounds, our moral obligations to one another.
transcript.zh: 要不是你在那所学校，校长根本不会专门为登上荣誉榜的孩子设立表彰早餐会。Nikole 从宏观讲到细节——孩子们结交不同背景的朋友带来的益处，还有我们彼此之间应尽的道德责任。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: Najya is not waiting for her to be done. She's jumping in. Opportunities for all kids, like what? You made friends with different kinds of people. Who? Dad being involved had a big impact? How?
transcript.zh: Najya 没等她把话说完就直接插话反问：给所有孩子提供机会，比如什么？说结交了各种背景的朋友，谁啊？爸爸参与学校事务产生了很大影响，怎么影响的？

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: We don't have to actually agree. It's okay for us to see this in a different way. But ultimately, you got into your first choice of high school.
transcript.zh: 其实我们没必要非得达成一致。我们对这件事看法不同也很正常。但说到底，你还是考进了自己的第一志愿高中。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: But you could have had me way higher in education.
transcript.zh: 可你原本能让我在学业上走得高得多。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Do you feel like your life is being held back?
transcript.zh: 你觉得自己的人生因此被耽误了吗？

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I don't think that, but I don't want to be—I didn't want to feel like I didn't know anything because I was set back in other schools. I didn't want to feel like I was dumb.
transcript.zh: 我倒不是这么觉得，可我不想——我不想因为之前那些学校拖了后腿，就觉得自己什么都不懂。我不想觉得自己像个傻瓜。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: In ninth grade, I did feel like I was dumb. It did feel like I didn't know anything. It was like, oh my gosh, you're like a dumb Black girl in a white school.
transcript.zh: 九年级的时候，我真的觉得自己笨极了，真的觉得自己一无所知。那种感觉就像，天哪，你就像是白人学校里那个蠢笨的黑人女孩。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Mm-hmm.
transcript.zh: 嗯。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: That's what it made me feel. Why should I have to suffer with that? Why couldn't you just benefit kids in another way? There was other options.
transcript.zh: 这就是它带给我的感受。为什么非得让我去承受这些？你为什么不能换种方式去帮那些孩子？明明有别的选择。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I don't think you can change—I think we have decades of people saying they were going to change a school from the outside, and I don't think—I just don't think you do.
transcript.zh: 我不认为你能从外部改变——几十年来一直有人说要从外部去改变一所学校，但我觉得……我觉得那根本行不通。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I think New York City is full of people who write checks and people who say, I believe in equality. I mean, what we were trying to do was not just about giving some additional funds to a school. We were trying to change the power dynamics.
transcript.zh: 我觉得纽约市到处都是开支票捐款的人，到处都是口口声声说“我相信平等”的人。我的意思是，我们想做的不只是给学校多拨点经费，我们想改变的是背后的权力格局。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: But that doesn't connect to why. Why did I have to be in the school?
transcript.zh: 可这还是没解释为什么。为什么非得由我去上那所学校？

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: Nikole says, okay, remember what happened in fourth grade when kids weren't being taught? Do you remember that? That wasn't just happening to you.
transcript.zh: Nikole 说，好吧，还记得四年级时老师根本不教课那件事吗？你还记得吗？那可不只是发生你一个人身上。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: The only way, though, that we know that's happening is because we're in the class and we're in the school. And had we not been in the school, we wouldn't have ever known that that was happening.
transcript.zh: 但我们之所以能发现那种情况，唯一的原因就是我们在那个班里、在那所学校里。如果我们不在那所学校，就永远不会知道正在发生这种事。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: There are ways that you could know that kind of stuff.
transcript.zh: 总有别的办法能知道这种事的。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: But there aren't. And we've talked about over and over, our lives are the products of people who didn't just say, we think segregation is wrong, we think injustice is wrong. They were willing to put themselves, their—
transcript.zh: 可根本没有别的办法。而且我们一遍又一遍地聊过，我们今天的生活之所以能这样，正是因为过去有这样一群人——他们不只是嘴上说说“我们认为种族隔离不对、不公不对”，他们愿意把自己、把自己的——

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: ...families, their children on the line for that.
transcript.zh: ……把自己的家人、自己的孩子都押上去。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: So you put me on the line to help a school, but it didn't work.
transcript.zh: 所以你把我押了上去，想去帮那所学校，结果根本没用。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Yeah, I put you on the line in hopes of making a change, yeah.
transcript.zh: 对，我是把你押了上去，希望能带来一点改变。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: But even—even when you knew—
transcript.zh: 可就算……就算你当时明知道——

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: It's not like I never had any doubts about my choice. I did. And the only reason I'm okay with my choice now is I'm like, you're fine.
transcript.zh: 我也不是从来没怀疑过自己的决定。我怀疑过。而我现在之所以能坦然面对这个选择，唯一的原因就是我觉得，你现在挺好的。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I felt this was important. I tried to do the right thing.
transcript.zh: 我觉得这件事很重要。我只是努力去做我认为对的事。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And I think I'm fine because I'm in the school I am now. I feel like if I picked a different choice that you wanted me to, I don't think I would be fine.
transcript.zh: 而我觉得我现在之所以挺好的，是因为我去了现在这所学校。要是当初我照你的意思选了另一条路，我觉得我现在根本好不了。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Okay.
transcript.zh: 好吧。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And I think this choice was good for me. And I do appreciate you for saying that.
transcript.zh: 我觉得我自己的选择很适合我。而且你刚刚能这么说，我真的很感激。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I think your choice is good for you as well.
transcript.zh: 我也觉得你的选择很适合你。

transcript.speaker: Najya Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Yes.
transcript.zh: 嗯。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: They'd done it. Nikole had committed to letting Najya have her say. She felt she owed it to her. And Nikole was committed to putting all of this out into the world.
transcript.zh: 她们做到了。Nikole 之前下定决心，要让 Najya 把心里话全说出来，她觉得这是自己欠女儿的。Nikole 也打定主意，要把这一切都公之于众。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: And as a final step in this whole process, she fact-checked herself. And she was in for a shock.
transcript.zh: 而作为整件事的最后一步，她核查了一下自己的记忆是否准确。结果，眼前的一切让她大吃一惊。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: Let's give this an act, a mini act, a postscript. Act Five: The Evidence.
transcript.zh: 我们干脆给这部分单设一幕吧，算是一个迷你幕、一段后记：Act Five——证据。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: She was checking her memory on things as she wrote her story for The New York Times Magazine. And Nikole looked through old emails back and forth with Najya's schools, messages to principals and teachers raising concerns.
transcript.zh: 当时她正为《纽约时报杂志》撰写这篇报道，顺便核对记忆里的细节。Nikole 翻出了以前和 Najya 所在学校来往的旧邮件，里面全是她写给校长和老师、反映各种问题的消息。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And there's pages of emails. I don't even remember sending that many emails. And I'm a writer and I'm a journalist, so my emails are very detailed.
transcript.zh: 邮件多得能铺满好几页。我甚至都不记得自己发过这么多邮件。而且我是个作家，也是个记者，所以我每封邮件都写得极其详细。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Every time I'm emailing the principal, I'm quoting my daughter, I'm listing all these details, the issues we were having, not feeling like we were getting the proper response, my worries, my concerns.
transcript.zh: 每次给校长写信，我都会引用我女儿的原话，把各种细节、我们遇到的问题、感觉一直没得到妥善回应的状况，还有我的忧虑和担心，一条条全列出来。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Like, Najya came home and said that her teacher was gone again, and this is the fourth time the teacher was gone, and there was no sub, and Najya said she had to go in the kindergarten class, but she's in second grade, right?
transcript.zh: 比如说，Najya 回家告诉我，她的老师又没来上课，这已经是老师第四次缺勤了，而且连个代课老师都没有，Najya 说她被安排去学前班教室待着——可她明明已经上二年级了，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And not just a record of my making complaints, but a record of non-caring—like the principal not responding, the teachers not responding over and over and over and over again.
transcript.zh: 那些邮件记录下的，不只是我一次次的投诉，更是一种彻底的漠不关心——校长不回邮件，老师也不回邮件，一次又一次，没完没了。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And I'm in Texas that day, and I'm getting ready to go give a talk, and I'm sitting in the hotel room and I'm just reading all of these emails. And it was crushing to read them.
transcript.zh: 那天我人正在得克萨斯州，准备去作一场演讲。我坐在酒店房间里，就那样一封接一封地读着这些邮件。读到这些的时候，我整个人都要崩溃了。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And I was like, damn, you really—to make this work for yourself, mentally I just forgot. I had just pushed a lot of that out of my memory, I think, to be able to live with the choices we were trying to make.
transcript.zh: 我当时就在想，天哪，你为了让自己心里能接受，竟然真的……在心理上把这些事给忘了。我想，我是把很多那样的记忆硬生生压了下去，这样才能心安理得地接受我们当时试图做出的那些选择。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And I understand my child feeling very betrayed by our choices.
transcript.zh: 现在我完全理解，为什么我的孩子会觉得自己被我们的选择深深背叛了。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: This is why my baby is so angry.
transcript.zh: 这就是为什么我的宝贝女儿会这么愤怒。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: Did you tell her any of that?
transcript.zh: 这些话你跟她说了吗？

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: Well, she calls me. She calls me right as I'm sitting there. I'm sitting at my desk, just going through all these emails, and I'm not crying, but I'm teary-eyed. I'm just sitting there.
transcript.zh: 结果她刚好给我打电话了。就在我坐在那儿的时候。我坐在书桌前翻看所有这些邮件，虽然没哭出声，但眼眶已经湿了，整个人就那样愣坐在那儿。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: So she calls me, and I pick up, and I'm trying to make my voice sound normal, but she hears that I'm upset in my voice. And she's like, what's wrong, Mommy? And I'm like, nothing, everything's good. And she's like, what's wrong?
transcript.zh: 她打来电话，我接起来，努力想让自己的声音听起来正常一点，但她还是从我的声音里听出我难过了。她就问：“妈妈，怎么了？”我说：“没事，一切都挺好的。”她又问：“到底怎么了？”

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And she asked me that maybe one more time, and then I just told her. I was like, I've been reading the emails from everything that was happening with your schools, and I'm sorry.
transcript.zh: 她大概又追问了一遍，然后我就全告诉她了。我说：“我一直在翻看以前关于你学校发生那些事的邮件，对不起。”

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And I just told her, I don't feel like you got the education you deserved, and I don't feel that I listened to you enough. I just said, I'm sorry.
transcript.zh: 我跟她说：“我觉得你没有得到你应得的教育，我也觉得自己以前没有足够认真地听你说话。”我就这么跟她说：“对不起。”

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: What did she say?
transcript.zh: 她怎么说的？

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: She was quiet for a second, and then she told me, I'm kind of glad you're seeing this now because I don't feel like you listened to me.
transcript.zh: 她沉默了一秒钟，然后对我说：“你现在能看到这些，我其实还挺欣慰的，因为我以前真的觉得你没有在听我说话。”

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I don't feel like you tried to understand that. And I just apologized again, and I said—
transcript.zh: “我觉得你那时候根本没试着去理解我的感受。”于是我又道了一次歉，我说——

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: You're right. The stakes were so high for me personally.
transcript.zh: 你说得对。对我个人来说，这里面的分量太重了。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I feel like the stakes are so high when it comes to the issue of integration and equality that I couldn't admit to her that, yes, you did bear a cost.
transcript.zh: 在种族融合与教育平等这件事上，我觉得赌注实在太大，以至于我一直没法向她承认：没错，你确实为此付出了代价。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And I don't know that we made the right choice. I don't know what the right choice would be.
transcript.zh: 我不知道我们当初的选择到底对不对。我也不知道，什么才算是正确的选择。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: I was stunned by this turn. I have never heard Nikole talk like this.
transcript.zh: 这个转折让我震惊。我从未听过 Nikole 这样说话。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: I've never heard most people, my closest friends, be this truthful with themselves about their choices, especially when it comes to our kids and schools.
transcript.zh: 我也从未见过身边大多数人，哪怕是我最亲密的朋友，在面对自己的选择时能如此坦诚地剖析自己——尤其是在关乎孩子和择校的问题上。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: And talking about those choices in public? Never. Why? So all of us can judge, or feel smug, or angry, or vindicated, or however you have felt listening to this?
transcript.zh: 更别提把这些选择摊开在公众面前谈论了，根本不可能。图什么呢？好让我们所有人去评头论足、暗自得意、义愤填膺、觉得自己早有先见之明，或者像你听这个故事时产生过的任何情绪吗？

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: It's not like Nikole is the only one out here making a choice. We all live in the same world she lives in.
transcript.zh: 现实中做选择的又不止 Nikole 一个人。我们和她生活在同一个世界里。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: We all live with schools that are segregated and unequal. We all make choices, imperfect, complicated choices.
transcript.zh: 我们都面对着同样存在种族隔离和不平等的学校系统，我们每个人都在做着不完美又无比复杂的选择。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: Nikole's just the one who's reckoning with hers, deeply and in public. And I think the less you talk about a choice, the less you scrutinize it, the easier it is to live with.
transcript.zh: 只不过 Nikole 是那个在公众面前、深刻反思自己选择的人。而且我觉得，对于自己做过的选择，聊得越少、审视得越少，心里反而越好受。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: Nikole is in a strange, new, and disorienting place these days. She's a person who's used to making an argument, and now she's not sure what to argue for.
transcript.zh: 如今的 Nikole 处在一个陌生、未知又让人迷茫的境地。她向来习惯于抛出清晰的论点，而现在，她却不知道自己还能为什么立场而辩护了。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: Not just because of her experience with Najya, also because of what Nikole's seen in her reporting over the last decade.
transcript.zh: 这不仅是因为她与 Najya 的这段经历，也是因为过去十年间她在新闻报道中所见证的一切。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: For years, Nikole's writing pushed for systemic change. In particular, she's argued that we need to integrate public schools racially and economically.
transcript.zh: 多年来，Nikole 一直通过写作推动系统性的变革。尤其是她一直主张，我们必须在种族和经济层面上推动公立学校的融合。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: And in her reporting, she's talked to so many people who put their lives into that fight, who sacrificed, made real, life-changing sacrifices that they hoped would lead to a bigger transformation.
transcript.zh: 而在她的报道中，她采访过太多把一生都投入到这场抗争里的人，他们做出了实实在在、甚至改变人生轨迹的牺牲，只盼着能换来一场更大的变革。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: And so little has changed. Public schools are unequal and segregated as they were 10 years ago, 30 years ago, 60 years ago.
transcript.zh: 可现实却几乎没有改变。公立学校依然像 10 年前、30 年前、60 年前那样，充斥着不平等与隔离。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: If you sacrifice to make a change, but change doesn't come, all you're left with is the sacrifice.
transcript.zh: 如果你为了改变而付出牺牲，可改变却迟迟没有到来，那最后留给你的，就只剩下牺牲本身。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And so what am I arguing for? I don't know anymore.
transcript.zh: 所以，我到底在主张什么呢？我也不知道了。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: Whoa, Nikole.
transcript.zh: 天哪，Nikole。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I know.
transcript.zh: 我知道。

transcript.speaker: Chana Joffe-Walt
transcript.en: A lot's happened.
transcript.zh: 发生了太多事。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: A lot has happened. The base of the argument is that what we are doing to Black children is immoral.
transcript.zh: 确实发生了太多事。不过，我论点的根基依然是：我们如今对黑人孩子所做的一切是不道德的。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: And that I have not wavered on, I will not waver on. I want us to understand that we choose this.
transcript.zh: 这一点我从未动摇，也绝不会动摇。我希望我们能明白，这一切都是我们自己选择的。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I don't want us to be absolved by it, not even me. I want us to come at the end of this story sharing my sense of devastation.
transcript.zh: 我不希望我们从中获得什么宽恕，连我自己也不例外。我希望我们走到这个故事的最后时，大家都能感受到我内心的那种痛彻心扉。

transcript.speaker: Nikole Hannah-Jones
transcript.en: I feel like the culmination of all my work is I'm going to force you to bear witness to what you choose and what I choose.
transcript.zh: 我觉得我毕生工作的归宿，就是要迫使你们直面并见证——你们做出了怎样的选择，而我又做出了怎样的选择。

transcript.zh: 本期节目由 Nancy Updike 制作并剪辑，Ira Glass 协助完成。

transcript.zh: 我们的执行编辑是 Sarah Abdurrahman，资深编辑是 David Kestenbaum，执行主编是 Emanuele Berry。

transcript.zh: Nikole 的那篇文章名为《In Fighting for Every Black Child, Did I Betray My Own?》，大家可以在《纽约时报》网站上阅读，文章编辑为 Ilena Silverman。今天还要特别感谢 Rachel Lissy。
